summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with a long history of poorly controlled type II diabetes, was admitted due to palpitations and shortness of breath caused by diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA). She had not taken her insulin or metformin for several weeks due to cost concerns and needle phobia. Upon admission, her blood glucose was critically high at 717 mg/dL with ketonuria and an elevated anion gap. She was treated with IV fluids and an insulin drip, which rapidly corrected her metabolic abnormalities. Electrolyte imbalances, including low sodium, magnesium, and phosphate, were addressed. Her condition stabilized, and she was transitioned to subcutaneous insulin. A diabetes management team adjusted her regimen, and social work assisted with medication access. She was discharged home on a new insulin protocol with instructions to monitor blood glucose twice daily and continue metformin. Follow-up with her primary care provider was arranged.
problems: Diabetes with ketoacidosis, type II or unspecified type, uncontrolled
